# 25 — Analyzers skip generated code — a `// <auto-generated>` marker silences 18 of 19 rules

**The GitHub issue is the authority. This document is a starting point only, and the GitHub issue always supersedes it.**

State: OPEN
Labels: none
Link: https://github.com/4thWAIV/agent-guard/issues/25

---

From the lockdown+coverage DESIGN sweep (2026-08-11). Tim: handle a different way, but record it as a known hole.

18 of 19 analyzers call `ConfigureGeneratedCodeAnalysis(GeneratedCodeAnalysisFlags.None)` — the lone exception is AG0008 (InteropOnlyInCrossPlatformLibrariesAnalyzer), whose own comment explains why .None is dangerous. `.None` tells Roslyn to skip any file/member it treats as generated (an `<auto-generated>` header, a `*.g.cs` name, or `[GeneratedCode]`). A lazy pass can mark a file/type as generated and every one of those 18 rules goes silent on it — defeating the whole fence on that file.

Candidate fix (was AG0027): require every analyzer to call `ConfigureGeneratedCodeAnalysis(.Analyze)`. To be handled a different way per Tim — record the hole.
